posts.text: Congress needs to pass strong kids’ safety rules and make these platforms responsible for the products they build so they stop blaming parents. It’s not the parents. It’s the products.
posts.summary: Demands Congress regulate social media platforms to protect children

posts.text: Parents shouldn’t have to fight Big Tech alone. We need rules of the road to hold tech companies accountable and protect kids.

posts.quote: Parents shouldn’t have to fight Big Tech alone. We need rules of the road to hold tech companies accountable and protect kids.

posts.text: I’ve been taking on social media companies for years — from passing the bipartisan TAKE IT DOWN Act to stop the spread of sexually explicit deepfakes on social media to fighting to open the courtroom doors to parents harmed by Meta’s constant push to make money no matter the harm.
posts.summary: Highlights record of challenging social media companies on harms

posts.text: Meta has finally agreed to put in place critical reforms to its platform like time limits on social media and restrictions on push notifications, and it will pay $17 billion for the harm it caused.

The recent cyberattacks on Minnesota water systems highlight the urgent need to protect our critical infrastructure.
 
That's why I introduced the Water Cyber Shield Act to help local water systems strengthen their cybersecurity and defend against threats.
posts.summary: Introduced bill to strengthen water system cybersecurity defenses

posts.text: Our members are simply asking for the two-year delay so all states will be on the same footing in working to reduce their error rates. That is ten percent of the total SNAP cuts.
posts.summary: Seeks SNAP delay equitably across states with varying error rates
posts.quote: Our members are simply asking for the two-year delay so all states will be on the same footing in working to reduce their error rates. That is ten percent of the total SNAP cuts.

posts.text: It still advantages high error rate states over states with mid-level error rates. A state with an error rate twice that of Minnesota will pay nothing in the second year, whereas states that have reduced their error rates will still be disadvantaged over high error rate states.
posts.summary: Argues SNAP cuts unfairly disadvantage states with low error rates

posts.text: I also appreciate that the Chairman has acknowledged the problem with the SNAP cost shift to states and counties. But amid tariff-related rising grocery prices in states across the country where SNAP has been critical, this is only a one-year fix.
posts.summary: Pushes for longer SNAP relief amid tariff-driven grocery price increases

Our democracy depends on free & fair elections.
 
The President’s Attorney General nominee Todd Blanche should be able to definitively say that he would not deploy armed federal agents to polling places, but he didn't.
 
I oppose his nomination.
